messages:
maria-support: FYI customer Acme reporting large latency (3-5s) and a sudden token billing spike this morning. They say they have a dedicated EU pool pinned but traces show requests routed to hosted-us. Can someone triage?

kai-eng-oncall: On it. Which cluster/region did they pin to? Any customer id?

maria-support: customer_id: acme-corp-42, pinned region: eu-west-1. Reported around 09:02 UTC. They attached a few request IDs: r-8a3c, r-8a4f, r-8b10.

alex-infra: grabbing routing logs now for acme-corp-42. Quick check: our routing manager shows recent capacity blips in eu-west-1 at 09:01:55 (short window) then a fallback decision to hosted-us1. Looks like fallback triggered before TTL refresh completed.

seb-runtime: can you paste the routing entry? I want to see fallback_reason and pool selection.

alex-infra: pasted snippet from routing debug:
```
route_key: acme-corp-42
selected_pool: hosted-us1
fallback_reason: dedicated_capacity_reported_zero
cache_ttl: 22s
last_capacity_report: 2024-08-09T09:01:55Z
server_reported_capacity: 0
```

maria-support: customer insists they had plenty of capacity. They ran a short autoscale at 08:59 and said all GPUs were healthy.

sara-telemetry: metric note: provisioner-heartbeat from dedicated-eu nodes showed a transient 400ms scheduling lag at 09:01:53 which coincides with that capacity report. The aggregator then emitted capacity=0 for one poll interval.

seb-runtime: hypothesis: small heartbeat hiccup caused the capacity aggregator to publish a 0, our router used that to flip to fallback. The routing cache TTL and the fallback gating logic then allowed a window where requests were sent to hosted-us. If the TTL refresh is jittered, we can get cross-region bridging.

kai-eng-oncall: Do we have a repro path? Can we simulate a 1-poll zero capacity and observe routing?

alex-infra: repro steps that matched customer behavior:
1) start dedicated-eu test fleet (3 nodes)
2) kill one node's heartbeat for 1.5s
3) run 50 concurrent requests with X-Region: eu-west-1 header
Observed ~7% routed to hosted-us1 and latency spike on those requests.

maria-support: customer provided a curl they used, posting here for repro:
```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Region-Preference: eu-west-1" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

seb-runtime: root cause candidate: routing TTL refresh + fallback threshold is too aggressive for single-poll zeros. Also an ordering bug: when capacity datapoint comes in with timestamp == last_poll and server reported 0 but next poll recovers, we still mark pool as unavailable until TTL expiry. Fix: add short hysteresis (require 2 consecutive zero polls within 30s window) or treat single-poll zeros as degraded not fully unavailable.

kai-eng-oncall: Agree. Short-term mitigation for Acme: we can force a pin override via the admin route API so their traffic stays on dedicated-eu even through a single poll blip.

alex-infra: admin pin override command (internal):
```bash
curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/v1/pinning -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 -d '{"customer":"acme-corp-42","region":"eu-west-1","force":true}'
```
I applied it at 09:12 UTC for a temporary 1h window.

maria-support: sent note to Acme that we forced a temporary pin and are rolling a fix. They want ETA and whether billing will be rebalanced for hosted traffic.

raj-billing: flagged the request. We'll trace the spike and open a billing adjustment ticket if it was caused by our routing fallback. Need exact counts of hosted tokens and timestamps.

seb-runtime: patch ready: routing:ignore-single-poll-zeros, commit 0a1b2c3, adds 2-sample hysteresis + lower the TTL jitter. I'll open PR and request urgent deploy to hotfix channel. Expected impact minimal.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: staging routing-service hotfix 0a1b2c3 -> started rollout to canary (1/5) at 09:24 UTC.

kai-eng-oncall: Plan: 1) keep admin pin for Acme for 1h 2) push hotfix to routing-service + monitor 3) if no regressions, finish rollout to prod 09:40-09:50 UTC 4) billing to review adjustments. Assigning seb-runtime + alex-infra.

seb-runtime: doing canary validation now. Observability: adding a short-latency metric for 'pin-override' decisions and 'fallback-count' by region.

alex-infra: note: double-checked our auth layer — tokens with region scope were fine; this was purely routing selection, not auth. Good to confirm.

maria-support: Acme confirmed they're back to normal after pin and canary looks good. They asked for a postmortem and whether we can prevent future cross-region token billing surprises.

raj-billing: will prepare billing impact and proposal for credits if hosted usage > baseline by >10% during the incident window.

seb-runtime: opening a small postmortem draft in #postmortems after prod rollout. Root cause: transient heartbeat/publish race -> single-poll zero -> aggressive fallback -> TTL jitter allowed cross-region flows. Remediation: hysteresis, TTL tuning, and a safety check to prefer pinned-dedicated for N minutes after a single blip.

kai-eng-oncall: Good. I'll keep watching the routing metrics for the next 2 hours and will ping if anything odd. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

maria-support: I'll close the customer's escalations after we share the postmortem and confirm billing follow-up. Thanks everyone.
